$comment: help-system policy — the machine-readable half of governance/help-system-policy.md,
read by scripts/check-help-conformance.mjs (gate-help-conformance). The prose policy is
the law a human reads; this file is the subset a gate can enforce without judgement.
WHY A POLICY FILE AND NOT CONSTANTS IN THE SCRIPT.
Same idiom as governance/frames-first-policy.json and governance/*-policy.json: the
strength of each check lives in a reviewed file, so tightening the help gate (flipping a
freshness ramp, adding a forbidden term) is a visible, owned diff rather than a code change
buried in the gate. The ramp pattern mirrors gate-ds-conformance / gate-frames-first.
WHAT THIS GATE EXISTS TO STOP (it has already happened once).
frontend/src/pages/HelpPage.tsx shipped to production calling the product 'FrontFuse',
hard-coding http://localhost:3001 as the API host, telling developers to
'npm install @frontfuse/sdk' (a package that does not exist — the scope is @fuzefront),
giving Netlify/Vercel/AWS deploy steps for a platform that deploys via Kubernetes/Helm/Argo,
and pointing support at support@frontfuse.dev / discord.gg/frontfuse / github.com/your-org.
Every one of those was a typeable, greppable, deterministic defect. This gate greps for
them so that class of rot cannot ship again.
docs/help/manifest.json is the index of record. Coverage is bidirectional: every article
the manifest lists must exist on disk, and every published article on disk must be listed.
An orphan article (on disk, unlisted) is invisible to the help UI and the dev portal; a
dangling entry (listed, missing) is a dead nav item. Both are hard failures.
Every published help article (docs/help/**/ *.md, excluding README.md and _*) carries YAML
frontmatter. These fields are load-bearing: the help UI renders from them, the gate checks
them, and `owner`/`lastReviewed` are what make a stale article findable instead of rotting.
Case-insensitive substrings that must never appear in a help content surface. Each has a
reason so a reviewer sees WHY, and an optional `allowIn` list of path globs where the term
is legitimate (e.g. a changelog noting the old name). The deterministic defect list — add to
it whenever a wrong-but-greppable fact is found in help content.

$comment: Regexes matched against every http(s):// URL found in a content surface. These catch
placeholder and localhost hosts that must not appear in PUBLISHED help, even if the exact
string is not on the forbiddenTerms list.

entries.reason: Localhost host in published help — use a same-origin relative path or a real host.

$comment: Markers that mean 'unfinished'. Allowed in status: draft articles; a hard failure in a
status: published article. 'No placeholders in published help' is the single rule that
separates a help center from a scaffold.
An article whose `lastReviewed` is older than `days` is stale. RAMP: mode=warn reports it
without failing (where the repo starts — no article should be failed for age the day the
gate lands); flip to mode=fail once the backlog of stale articles is zero and an owner
accepts that every future PR touching a stale article must re-review it. Mirrors the
gate-ds-conformance / gate-frames-first ramp. Owner decides the flip.
Visual media (screenshots, screencasts) live under assetDir, referenced from an article's
frontmatter `media:` list as { src, alt, type }. The gate enforces: the asset exists on
disk, every image/video has non-empty alt/caption text (accessibility), the extension is
allowed, and no committed asset is a placeholder (0-byte, or name matching a placeholder
marker). Producing the actual recordings is tracked in Jira, not faked in-repo — so this
section is enforced-but-mostly-empty until real assets land, which is deliberate.
maxImageKB keeps the repo from accreting multi-MB uncompressed PNGs; the media standard in
the policy doc says how to capture and compress. Video is NOT committed to git — it is
hosted (see policy doc 'Media standard'); the gate allows a video media entry whose src is
an https URL to an approved host and whose type is 'video'.
Relative markdown links between help files must resolve to a file that exists. External
https links are NOT fetched by the gate (CI must not depend on the network and must not be
a request amplifier) — external-link rot is caught by the scheduled doc-validity job, not
this per-PR gate. forbiddenUrlPatterns above still statically rejects placeholder hosts.
Globs excluded from content checks entirely (not from manifest coverage). README.md files
and the _assets tree are infrastructure, not articles.
